title: A week of careful speech
hook: no gossip, no harsh words, for seven days
tomorrow: soldiers lead a man out. he stops to touch the doorpost. why?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the third pillar the world stands on: kindness, for rich and poor, with your hands as well as your money. One kindness a day. Today, the tool you use for kindness most often: your mouth.
screen: `ONE KINDNESS A DAY.` → `THE TOOL YOU USE MOST.`

segments.voice: A group chat lights up with a screenshot and a row of crying-laughing faces. Nobody's lying. It's just about someone who isn't in the chat. There's a rabbi who wrote a whole book about that moment, and he's known by its title, two words from a Psalm: Chafetz Chaim, desiring life. The Psalm asks, "Who is the man that desireth life, and loveth days, that he may see good therein?" Its answer is about the mouth.
screen: `A SCREENSHOT AND A ROW OF LAUGHING FACES.` → `TWO WORDS: DESIRING LIFE.` → `THE ANSWER IS ABOUT THE MOUTH.`

segments.voice: Here's the next line: "Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile." The book is about lashon hara, the evil tongue: saying something negative about a person who isn't there, even when it's true. True is the surprising part. Being accurate doesn't make it kind. And notice where the Psalm files it: not under manners, under the question of life itself. Whoever wants good days starts with the tongue. So a week of careful speech is easy to say and hard to keep: no gossip, no harsh words, for seven days, and a tally when you slip. Now hold this week's rule up to the light. A coin in the pushke: a coin a week. Ten minutes on the calendar: fix a time. Isaac in his field: the middle of the day. The merchant at the till: look back kindly. Mar Zutra in bed: forgive before sleeping. The world's third pillar: one kindness a day. And now the mouth, the tool you carry everywhere.
screen: `KEEP THY TONGUE FROM EVIL.` · `LASHON HARA: EVEN WHEN IT'S TRUE.` · `SEVEN DAYS, AND A TALLY.` · `A WEEK OF THE RULE.` · then, large: `SEVEN DAYS OF CLEAN SPEECH.`

segments.voice: Hold up one hand, fingers open. Go back through today's conversations and fold one finger down for each time you said something about someone who wasn't there. No verdicts, just the count; then open your hand again and rest it on your knee.
screen: `ONE HAND, FINGERS OPEN.` · `FOLD ONE FOR EACH.` · `NO VERDICTS. JUST THE COUNT.`

segments.voice: A week of careful speech: seven days with no lashon hara and no harsh words, kept with a simple tally.
screen: `A WEEK OF CAREFUL SPEECH — today's word`.

segments.voice: Hold on to this one: seven days of clean speech. One hand, one tally, and nobody talked about who isn't there.

screen: `DAY 1659 COUNTS.` → `A RULE OF LIFE · 12 OF 15.` → `TOMORROW: HE STOPS TO TOUCH THE DOORPOST. WHY?`

howItsDone: Some Jews study a short daily portion of the Chafetz Chaim's laws of speech, and some schools and families take on 'speech weeks' or a set hour each day free of lashon hara.
